text:
nisha: opening a focused follow-up thread after last night's OOM on inference-prod-4. postmortem doc has root cause sketch but we need concrete owners, timelines, and a short-term mitigation plan that avoids emergency capacity increases.

omar: quick summary from heap artifacts: per-session KV grew to ~120MB on a handful of long-running sessions. jemalloc stats show rising retained memory and many small freelist misses. traces -> s3://debug/1742094123/{heap,jemalloc,profiles}.

chris: tl;dr: pattern repeating (long sessions + chat-tool state accumulation). two angles: storage-side (prune/evict) and allocator-side (reduce retention). both needed.

Sylvie: proposed immediate steps (T+24h):
- enforce per-session soft cap at 30MB, soft->warn; hard cap at 80MB with trimming/reject.
- kill switch: a supervisor flag to auto-trim top-n KVs for sessions over 80MB.
- add an eviction policy: LRU with TTL for tool-generated entries.

nisha: we also want metrics so we detect recurrence: per-session kv_size gauge, host_retained_bytes, jemalloc fragmentation ratio. alert if >30MB for 3m or fragmentation ratio >1.3 for 5m.

dan: I'll take the cap+supervisor endpoint. will PR session-manager changes and expose an admin /trim endpoint. ETA: 48h.

omar: I'll run allocation profiles and try the `opt.retain:false` jemalloc experiment in staging. need perf baseline. ETA: 72h for data.

chris: QA/validation: add a daily e2e job that runs a scaled long-session test (6h run with 500 concurrent long sessions) to the eval pipeline. if kv growth observed, auto-file regression. I can add the k6 script.

sylvie: I'll own observability dashboards & alerts. will add the following panels: per-session kv distribution, top 100 sessions by kv, fragmentation trend, host RSS. alert rules will be in alert-manager. ETA: end of day tomorrow.

nisha: dependencies/risks: allocator change may affect p99 latency. plan: staging canary 10% -> 1h soak -> metrics. if p99 increases >10% revert.

dan: sample local repro commands added to ticket (use cgroup to simulate low memory):
```
# spawn long sessions
k6 run --vus 100 --duration 6h kv_long_run.js
# watch jemalloc
curl localhost:9100/debug/jemalloc | tee jemalloc.out
# trigger trim
curl -XPOST localhost:9001/admin/trim?limit=50MB
```

omar: also found fragmentation hotspots in tokenizer and tool-result serialization. small-allocation churn is the main culprit. suggest short-term pooling for serializer buffers.

chris: ownership summary (confirm):
- dan: implement hard/soft caps + /admin/trim endpoint + PR (ETA 48h)
- omar: jemalloc experiments + flamegraphs + pooling suggestion (ETA 72h)
- sylvie: dashboards & alerts (ETA 24h)
- chris: e2e regression job + k6 script (ETA 3 days)
- nisha: coordinate review, update incident runbook, and schedule follow-up check-in (ETA Fri)

sre-bot: created follow-up tasks: TASK-5310(dan), TASK-5311(omar), TASK-5312(sylvie), TASK-5313(chris), incident INC-2026-03-24-17 linked.

nisha: decision: ship soft cap + alerting first. hard cap + trim endpoint gated behind small staging canary. if we still see >2 hosts at risk, escalate capacity bump.

dan: opened WIP PR #6910 for cap + feature flag. linking here. please review.

omar: starting jemalloc A/B in staging with `MALLOC_CONF=opt.retain:false,background_thread:true,decay_time:1` on a 10% slice. will post memory + latency diffs.

sylvie: dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood/d/kv-oom/kv-oom-overview. alert rule `KV_SESSION_HIGH` created.

chris: added k6 script to repo and scheduled daily job in CI as `kv-long-nightly`. first run tomorrow.

nisha: please post short thread updates when you hit your milestones. we'll reconvene at the Friday ops sync and close tasks or escalate. thanks all. :pray:

sre-bot: task status updates: TASK-5310 -> in_progress, TASK-5311 -> queued, TASK-5312 -> done, TASK-5313 -> in_progress.

omar: quick note: if anyone spots immediate pressure, set `POOL_MAINTENANCE=true` on the pool to drain new sessions and avoid filling hosts.

nisha: adding runbook snippet to incident doc and pinging infra-oncall. once caps + alerts are in place, we'll remove emergency capacity plan.
